jobs.title: Deputy Director
jobs.description:
Hospitality House is an emergency shelter and housing provider serving low\-income and homeless residents in Nevada County. Hospitality House provides pathways to housing by bringing homeless residents into a compassionate circle of community care that offers shelter, housing resources, sustenance, opportunity, dignity, and hope as they transition from homelessness to housing.

We are seeking a strategic, mission\-driven Deputy Director to help lead our organization into its next chapter. This is a rare opportunity to step into a senior executive role with a clear, intentional pathway to the Executive Director position working side\-by\-side with our current Executive Director to shape agency strategy, strengthen programs, and build lasting community partnerships. If you are a seasoned nonprofit leader ready to grow into an executive director role while making a tangible difference for people experiencing homelessness in the Sierra Foothills, we invite you to apply.

Rate of Pay

$120,640 – $124,800 annually

**Benefits**

* Medical Insurance (100% of premium paid by the employer).
* Dental Insurance.
* Vision Insurance.
* Life Insurance.
* Long\-term Disability Insurance.
* Voluntary Short\-term Insurance.
* Voluntary Accident.
* Voluntary Critical Illness.
* 401k.
* 11 paid holidays.
* 11 paid sick days.
* Paid vacation days

**POSITION SUMMARY**

Hospitality House seeks a full\-time Deputy Director to help manage the day\-to\-day operations of the organization alongside the Executive Director. The Deputy Director is a senior executive\-level role providing strategic, operational, and programmatic oversight in close partnership with the Executive Director. The Deputy Director will directly supervise the Housing and Supportive Services Officer, the CalAIM Manager, and the Development team, while supporting programmatic divisions to ensure high\-quality services, regulatory compliance, and mission alignment. When needed, the Deputy Director will serve as the Acting Executive Director.

This role is intentionally structured as a succession pathway to the Executive Director position. The Deputy Director will receive mentorship and hands\-on training in governance, development, financial stewardship, human resources, and operations to build readiness to assume full organizational leadership.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership and Visioning**

* Partner with the Executive Director to design and implement the strategic framework that upholds Hospitality House's values, mission, and vision.
* Serve as a visible ambassador of the agency in community, regional, and state\-level collaborations, task forces, and public forums.
* Keep abreast of evolving best practices in homelessness services, program design, and regulatory compliance, bringing innovation back to the agency.

**Programmatic Oversight and Personnel Management**

* Provide direct supervision and mentorship to the Housing and Supportive Services Officer, CalAIM Manager, and Development Director, as well as other applicable staff.
* Ensure case management, shelter, outreach, and housing programs are delivered in alignment with best practices, contractual requirements, and agency standards.
* Support staff recruitment, training, and retention efforts to ensure consistent service quality.
* Partner with HR in staff development planning; conduct regular performance evaluations and recommend recognition/reward as appropriate.

**Grants, Contracts, Database Management, and CalAIM Compliance**

* Collaborate with the Director of Business Operations and other members of leadership to ensure effective data collection, reporting, and compliance for grants and contracts.
* Partner with Business Operations to monitor program budgets, reimbursements, and regulatory reporting obligations.
* Participate in proposal development and reporting processes to strengthen funding streams.

**Community Relations**

* Represent Hospitality House in collaborative partnerships with service providers, local government, funders, donors, and community stakeholders.
* Actively participate in education, outreach, and advocacy efforts to raise awareness of homelessness and the organization's impact.
* Strengthen Hospitality House's public profile by cultivating strong relationships with civic leaders, business partners, faith communities, and philanthropists.

**CalAIM Program Oversight**

* Provide leadership oversight of Hospitality House's CalAIM Program, ensuring compliance with state and federal regulations, contract requirements, and organizational policies.
* Supervise and support the CalAIM Manager, ensuring accurate and timely billing, audits, reporting, and data management.
* Partner with Business Operations, HR, and program leadership to ensure CalAIM staff are trained, resourced, and compliant with evolving CalAIM standards.
* Monitor performance and quality metrics, ensuring CalAIM services are delivered effectively, efficiently, and in alignment with best practices.
* Serve as a liaison with managed care plans, funders, and state/local agencies regarding CalAIM implementation and compliance.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director and leadership team to integrate CalAIM program outcomes into broader organizational strategy, sustainability planning, and funding requests.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non\-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions\-driven, passionate change\-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world\-wide for a better future.


We are committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. We are a dedicated advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Job Overview:**  

As the Development Director you will oversee the design, implementation, and monitoring of resource mobilization efforts in support of our mission. The specific areas of responsibility and oversight include: donor relations and reporting, collaboration with colleagues at IRC headquarters on a new collaborative fundraising structure for individual donors, outreach and prospecting to local corporate and private foundation donors, special events planning and oversight. As a member our region's senior leadership team, you will share responsibilities with other Directors for providing effective oversight over regional operations and good stewardship of resources. This is a full\-time exempt position, reporting to the Executive Director of the Sacramento/Turlock region.

**Major Responsibilities:**  

The Development Director works in close coordination with the Executive Director and local leadership to achieve the following goals:

* Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan with specific and measurable goals and objectives for development of restricted and unrestricted funds.
* Develop strategy for and execute special, restricted fundraising campaigns through digital and traditional channels, in partnership with HQ Mass Markets teams.
* Cultivate national partnerships from companies and foundations based in the Sacramento/Central Valley region, in coordination with HQ\-based Institutional Philanthropy \& Partnerships team.
* Support local high\-value donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship in close collaboration with USA Philanthropy team.
* Oversee the preparation of letters of inquiry, proposals, budgets and reports to local foundations and other potential donors in coordination with the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team, office leadership and HQ counterparts.
* Oversee joint initiatives with local programming to identify funding needs and create strategic plans to seek funding support for these needs.
* Organize annual fundraisers and other special events as applicable.
* Ensure development of strong corporate donor engagement opportunities that are aligned with program need and donor interest for national and local donors.
* Serve as focal point and liaison for Sacramento\-Turlock to HQ fundraising teams.
* Provide high level oversight for the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team.
* Coordinate with Resource \& Development Coordinators across the region to ensure consistency between volunteer and financial / in\-kind support.
* Assist in raising awareness about the IRC and representing the office at meetings, seminars, and forums.
* Recruit, hire, train and supervise development\-related interns and volunteers, when appropriate.
* Maintain ongoing communication on status of resource development initiatives and provide timely reports on management issues and concerns.
* Participate actively on Sacramento\-Turlock’s Leadership Team and collaborate closely with management team to ensure efficient collaboration with all offices in the delivery of quality services
* Work with Executive Director on opportunities to highlight the local and global work of IRC.
* Other tasks as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

* University degree (BA/BS) required; graduate degree in Development, Nonprofit Management or Business Management, or International Relations preferred
* Minimum of five (5\) years prior experience with leading fundraising, communications, public relations, and other development duties in the non\-profit sector required
* Impeccable attention to detail
* Experience with Salesforce strongly preferred
* Strong writing skills required
* Strong donor network in the Sacramento/Central Valley region preferred
* Demonstrated record of foundation and donor relations with successful development of private foundation grant proposals
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically with donors, volunteers, partner agencies, government officials, multi\-cultural clients and colleagues on all levels. Demonstrated ability to work successfully in a multi\-cultural environment.
* Experience coordinating multiple partners and consensus building toward common goal.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (especially Word, Excel, Outlook) and internet research
* Strong organizational, leadership and team\-building skills with ability to promote productivity and efficiency

**Working Environment:**


Hybrid work with minimum 3x/week in office. Standard office environment. Some travel to other regional offices required as well as to various venues for events and for meeting with donors. Availability for non\-traditional hours including weeknights and weekends on a limited basis required.  

  

**Compensation:** ($109,416 \- $117,354\). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience

jobs.description:
Education Program Director, Greater Good Education \#88470 About Berkeley
  
  

At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  

Departmental Overview
  
  

The Greater Good Science Center at UC Berkeley (GGSC) studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well\-being and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society. Over more than two decades, the GGSC has provided a bridge between scientists and the public, turning research findings into practical resources that support well\-being for all. Since its founding, the Center has highlighted the importance of building social connections not only within communities but across groups, offering practical strategies for overcoming bias and prejudice, expanding one's circle of care, and promoting diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
  
  

The GGSC's Greater Good Education (GGE) program provides education professionals with practical, scientific insights to help them integrate the science of well\-being and flourishing into their lives, schools, and classrooms. It draws on disciplines such as social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character education, and related topics. GGE's goal is to help education professionals better understand the roots of kind, helpful \- or "prosocial" \- behavior and emotional well\-being, and how they can build those skills in themselves, their colleagues, and their students.
  
  

GGE resources include our pioneering Greater Good in Education website, which offers more than 350 actionable, research\-based practices and has engaged several million users; a suite of online courses that support student and educator well\-being; Greater Good articles that share the latest education\-related research and its practical application in classrooms and schools; and Greater Good Educators, a community of practice program that brings together educators from around the world to learn with and from each other about the keys to individual and collective well\-being in education.
  
  

The GGSC's organizational culture prioritizes independence, rigor, and the well\-being of its members. Staff members enjoy autonomy and flexibility while working in a culture that encourages teamwork, connection, and collaboration. The GGSC welcomes a diversity of experiences and perspectives to inform its work and strives to operate internally by the values that drive its public\-facing programs: empathy, compassion, joy, forgiveness, appreciation, and cooperation. Recognizing that the science we cover has been shaped by systemic biases and inequities, we aim to address and correct for these prejudices whenever possible.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

This position serves as the Greater Good Education (GGE) Program Director, overseeing the program's mission to build kinder, happier schools where everyone belongs. This position leads the short\- and long\-term planning for GGE, shaping the program's goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model. Working closely with the GGSC's executive director, the Education Program Director manages fundraising for the program and ensures that the program's direction aligns with the GGSC's overall direction. This position supervises a team that includes the Associate Director, Program Coordinator, Director of Learning Communities, Director of Educational Partnerships, Marketing Specialist, and Communications Specialist.
  
  

The Education Program Director oversees all GGE program content, partnerships, and other activities, including training, evaluation, and communities of practice, while also overseeing the development of the new Greater Good Schools program, which focuses on integrating Greater Good values into the fabric of entire schools and districts. The successful candidate possesses extensive experience in K\-12 education and a strong grasp of the science of social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character development, and other prosocial research in education. Additionally, this position requires an entrepreneurial spirit and a command of nonprofit strategy, development, and management.
  
  

Application Review Date
  
  

The First Review Date for this job is September 22, 2026\. For full consideration, please apply by the first review date.
  
  

Responsibilities
  
  

Lead Program Strategy and Development
  
  

Lead short\- and long\-term strategic planning for Greater Good Education (GGE), shaping the program's goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model, in collaboration with the GGSC's executive director and GGE program staff.
  
Identify and pursue funding opportunities for GGE, working in concert with the GGSC's executive director, deputy director, and development director.

**ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW**

Founded in October of 1995, United Samaritans Foundation mission is to deliver food to people in need in Stanislaus County, and to facilitate the provision of services to assist them in a transition to a better quality of life.

In today’s economy, with housing costs, utilities and groceries climbing, earning a wage is no longer a guarantee of having enough to eat. United Samaritans Foundation serves the gap between what people earn and what life costs.

Revenues: $ 1\.9 million\~. For more information please visit: unitedsamaritans.org

**POSITION DESCRIPTION** 

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight for all organizational activities, ensuring alignment with the mission and vision.
* Serve as the primary representative of the organization to community partners, donors and the community.
* Develop and implement operational policies, procedures, and best practices to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
* Lead, motivate, and manage staff by providing guidance while delegating responsibilities appropriately.
* Oversee program development, expansion, and evaluation to ensure high\-quality service delivery.
* Collaborate closely with the Board of Directors to establish organizational goals, monitor progress, and report on performance.
* Foster a positive organizational culture that encourages innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with all legal, regulatory, and funding requirements.
* Drive fundraising efforts in partnership with development staff to support organizational sustainability.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Proven experience in executive leadership or senior management roles within a nonprofit or similar organization.
* Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to develop and execute long\-term plans.
* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills to effectively engage diverse stakeholders.
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities effectively, and build a collaborative work environment.
* In\-depth knowledge of organizational operations, program management, and industry\-specific best practices.
* Ability to develop a thorough understanding of the organization’s core programs and operational landscape.
* Experience working with a Board of Directors or governing body is preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in nonprofit management, public administration or related field is advantageous.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS** 

Successful candidates for this position will undergo background checks. Applicants will have an opportunity to discuss any adverse background information before a determination is made about its potential impact on their candidacy.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

The salary range for this position begins at $85,000 yearly, based on education and experience. The total compensation package includes health benefits, and 6 paid holidays.

**HOW TO APPLY**

To apply, submit a resume and cover letter. Your resume must not exceed two (2\) pages and should demonstrate how your experience meets the minimum qualifications for the position. Your cover letter must not exceed two (2\) pages and should describe why you are interested in the position and how your professional, education and personal experiences meet the desired attributes listed above.

For questions about the position or the application process or accommodations, please contact Linda at 209\.668\-4853 or email to: Linda@unitedsamaritans.org.

Pay: From $85,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

**DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT**


**ABOUT THE EBELL LOS ANGELES**



The Ebell of Los Angeles is a women\-led nonprofit organization that has served the Greater Los Angeles community for more than a century. Its mission is to inspire women and build community through arts, culture, education, service, and stewardship of its historic campus and collections. As The Ebell enters an ambitious new chapter, the organization is preparing to steward its historic landmark campus for its next century while expanding its philanthropic capacity and community impact.


**POSITION SUMMARY**



The Director of Development (DOD) is a seasoned, entrepreneurial leader responsible for building and scaling The Ebell's philanthropic program at a pivotal moment in the organization's history. Reporting directly to the CEO, the DOD will initially serve as the organization's lead frontline fundraiser, developing relationships with individual and institutional donors, making direct asks, and building a robust major gifts pipeline in support of annual, capital, and campaign priorities.



This is an opportunity for an experienced development professional to help create a culture of philanthropy across an organization where fundraising capacity and expertise are still evolving. The DOD will serve as a close partner and advisor to the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, helping organizational leaders become more effective ambassadors, relationship\-builders, and fundraisers.


**ROLES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**


*Fundraising \& Major Gifts*


* Serve as The Ebell's lead frontline fundraiser, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major individual and institutional donors, including six\- and seven\-figure prospects.
* Build and manage a robust major gifts pipeline, using disciplined prospect identification, cultivation, solicitation, moves management, and stewardship practices.

Jewish Long Beach is on a mission to strengthen community, deepen connection, and expand opportunity across three core pillars: the Jewish Community Foundation, the Jewish Federation, and the Alpert Jewish Community Center. With over $30 million in managed assets and nearly $2 million raised annually, Jewish Long Beach serves as both a steward of long\-term legacy giving and a driver of immediate community investment.

It's more than a job; it's a calling. It's where passion meets purpose. ADAPT Community Network, formerly United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) of NYC provides a multitude of services to people with developmental disabilities. At ADAPT, we are 3,000 strong, and it takes every one of us to empower the lives of the people we support. With caring and great resources at hand, we know what it takes to help people live fuller, happier, healthier lives. Our employees show their commitment to the people we support every day, and we all deliver on our promise to provide innovative and comprehensive services to individuals with developmental disabilities.


For your next career move, apply with us at ADAPT Community Network! Wherever you work among our many locations around New York City, ADAPT offers paid training, competitive benefits, and we foster a team culture of learning, support, collaboration and career growth.

**SUMMARY**


The Senior Director of Partnerships will be a key member of the fundraising and strategic growth success of the Marketing and Development Department. This position, under the direction of the Senior Vice President of Marketing and Fund Development, will lead the development, cultivation, and stewardship of corporate, foundation, community, and strategic partnerships. The Senior Director of Partnerships will be responsible for expanding revenue opportunities, strengthening external relationships, and advancing ADAPT Community Network's mission through meaningful collaborations and philanthropic investment.

jobs.description:
### **Description**

 **ABOUT BREAKTHROUGH NEW YORK**
Breakthrough New York empowers motivated students from low\-income communities to achieve a college degree and reach their fullest potential. Our tuition\-free program supports over 500 students and their families from 7th grade through college. We accept middle school students who are furthest from high\-quality educational opportunities yet show promise and potential: 99% of students identify as persons of color and 56% will be the first in their families to graduate college.  

As a ten\-year program, Breakthrough New York supports students and their families through key transition points in their academic journeys. We provide academic enrichment through summer and after\-school opportunities; coach students to gain admissions into selective high schools and colleges, and expose students to diverse interests and careers so they can shape their own trajectories.  

In addition to nurturing individual talent, we cultivate a thriving community of like\-minded peers and mentors who encourage each other’s ambitions and passions. Personalized mentorship and holistic support are signature elements of our model, with over 200 near\-peer seasonal staff and volunteers who work with students at each stage of our continuum.  

The Breakthrough model works: 94% of Breakthrough students enroll in college preparatory high schools, and 97% are on track to graduate from college in four\-six years. Learn more at Breakthrough New York's website. **ABOUT THE POSITION**
  

*Reporting directly to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), the Director of Grants and Communications Manager will join the development team to collaboratively raise an organizational budget of $4\.024M annually, and oversee a portfolio of $1\.2M \- $1\.5M current and prospective opportunities. This position is responsible for renewing and identifying new grants from institutional partners. As a skilled written communicator and project manager, they will work closely with the CDO and Executive Director to meet ambitious giving goals by managing and growing existing public, foundation, and corporate foundation funding, identifying and pursuing new funding opportunities, and supporting organization communications. This role is crucial for ensuring the organization's financial sustainability and ability to carry out Breakthrough New York’s mission effectively.*  

### **Key Responsibilities**

 *Grant Writing and Project Management (50%)** Craft compelling and thorough grant proposals and reports that effectively communicate the organization's mission, programs, and impact to current and potential institutional donors.
* Create standardized templates for grant proposals and reports to ensure consistency and efficiency for all development team usage.
* Curate and update a repository of approved language for proposals and program\-related pitch materials.
* Facilitate data requests to the Chief Program Officer, operations requests to the Senior Director of People Ops, and budget requests to accounting as necessary for grant applications and reporting.
* Establish review processes and timelines with the CDO and/or ED as needed for each grant report project to ensure quality and timeliness.
* Maintain a grants management calendar to track deadlines and ensure timely completion of all deliverables.

  

*Prospect Research and Portfolio Maintenance (25%)** Conduct prospect research to identify single and multi\-year institutional funding opportunities.
* Cultivate pathways for introductions to potential institutional donors and create prospect profiles for frontline fundraisers.
* Support the CDO and ED with maintaining relationships with institutional donors through regular communication, event invites, and impact updates.
* Work closely with program staff to understand funding needs and priorities, and align fundraising efforts with programmatic goals.
* Manage the financial aspects of institutional giving, including budgeting and forecasting for the portfolio.

  

*Communications (25%)** Partner with the full organizational team to write content for BTNY’s monthly newsletter, social media, and other external\-facing materials.
* Establish a community spotlight roster in collaboration with CDO, interview BTNY community members, write profiles and blog posts.
* Assist development team with written content for solicitation letters and proposals.

  

### **Skills, Knowledge and Expertise**

  

While these are not all requirements, the right candidate is likely to see themselves in the examples below. These examples are designed to help you determine if this opportunity aligns with your own strengths and sense of purpose.* You have exceptional writing and editing abilities, are capable of crafting compelling narratives that effectively communicate the organization's mission, goals, and impact to potential funders. You can adapt your writing style to meet varied funder needs.
* You have the ability to break down and sequence large projects into manageable pieces for yourself and others \- seeing the big picture, but executing on the details (i.e. developing and implementing project plans; creating and testing data collection instruments, writing and reviewing reports).
* You thrive in environments with tight deadlines, and manage your time efficiently to ensure that grant deliverables are submitted on time and accurately.
* You’ve demonstrated the ability to work diligently towards your goals and can comfortably pivot and try new strategies when challenges arise.
* You are a team player and value both external feedback and self\-reflection.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:*** Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
* Minimum of three years experience in grant writing and project management, preferably in the nonprofit sector.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively.
* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

**Position Title:** Development Director

**Location:** New York, NY (On\-site with hybrid flexibility)

**About the Peter Westbrook Foundation**

The Peter Westbrook Foundation (PWF) is a nationally recognized nonprofit that uses the sport of fencing to empower underrepresented youth through athletic excellence, academic support, and mentorship. With a legacy rooted in Olympic success and community impact, PWF is committed to developing champions both on and off the fencing strip.

**Position Summary**

PWF is seeking an experienced and strategic fundraising professional to lead its development efforts as Development Director. This senior leadership role will oversee all aspects of fundraising, including individual giving, corporate partnerships, foundation grants, special events, and donor stewardship. The Development Director will work closely with the CEO, board members, and program staff to secure and grow sustainable revenue streams to support PWF’s mission.

jobs.title: Executive Director - Mukti Mission US
jobs.description:
Executive Director \- Mukti Mission US
The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Mukti Mission US is the public face of MMUS, and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission, strengthening donor and ministry partnerships, overseeing operations, and providing leadership for fundraising, communications, and organizational development. The Executive Director reports directly to the US Board of Directors and works collaboratively with donors, churches, volunteers, ministry partners, and Mukti Mission leadership in India.  

  

  



**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**  

**Leadership and Administration**

* Provide leadership for the day\-to\-day operations of Mukti Mission US.
* Recruit, train, supervise, coordinate, and support paid staff.
* Responsible for staff culture, performance management, and leadership development.
* Create annual goals, plans, and priorities consistent with the mission and direction established by the Board. Responsible for strategic planning and execution with measurable goals.
* Ensure effective administrative systems, policies, and procedures.

**Fundraising and Donor Development**

* Develop and implement strategies to increase financial support for Mukti Mission.
* Cultivate and maintain relationships with individual donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and ministry partners, with a focus on expanding the donor base and strengthening long\-term giving. Also, responsible for spearheading fundraising campaigns.
* Encourage engagement through prayer, giving, advocacy, and volunteer service.
* Manage CRM database \& integrate donation platform to website for funding campaigns.

**Partnership and International Relations**

* Serve as the primary liaison between Mukti Mission US and Mukti Mission in India, and facilitate communication and partnership while respecting the governance and leadership structures of Mukti Mission in India.
* Maintain current knowledge of ministry activities, projects, and priorities in India.
* Foster collaborative relationships with international councils and/or Executive Directors.

**Volunteer and Mission Team Coordination**

* Recruit, train, and coordinate volunteers and local ambassadors serving Mukti Mission US.
* Facilitate short\-term service opportunities and ministry\-related travel to India, when appropriate, in partnership with Mukti India.
* Represent Mukti Mission US at international Council meetings (once every 3 years), along with at least one annual site visit, and any other key events as requested by the Board.

**Communications, Events, and Ministry Promotion**

* Oversee the development and distribution of publications, prayer updates, newsletters, electronic communications, annual donor giving statements, sponsorship letters, and promotional materials. Promote awareness of Mukti's ministry, impact, and needs.
* Ensure effective use of digital platforms, including website and social media channels.
* Represent Mukti Mission US through speaking engagements and tables at relevant meetings, conferences, etc. Also responsible for hosting the annual Muk\-Tea event.

**Board Relations and Governance**

* Support the Board of Directors in fulfilling its governance responsibilities.
* Prepare materials and reports for Board meetings in consultation with the Executive Committee, and provide regular monthly updates regarding ministry activities, finances, and organizational performance to the board. Assist in the implementation of Board\-approved initiatives.
* Regularly engage with the Board Executive Committee on key issues facing the ministry.

**Financial Oversight and Compliance**

* Oversee accurate financial records, budget development, cash\-flow, internal controls, and risk management. Monitor ministry\-sponsored projects and donor\-designated funds.
* Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
* Maintain compliance with applicable legal, financial, and accountability standards, including IRS, State \& Federal 501(c)3 regulations and registrations, ECFA, and Candid requirements.
* Work with Board Treasurer and External Auditor on reporting and accountability.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Genuine commitment to evangelical Christianity, and the mission and vision of Mukti Mission U.S.
* 8\-10 years of experience in nonprofit ministry leadership, cross\-cultural ministry, nonprofit financial management, and fundraising.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, and excellent interpersonal skills.
* Demonstrated experience building relationships with donors, churches, volunteers, and community partners.
* Demonstrated technical proficiency with digital communication tools, CRM database management, website management, etc.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including periodic travel to India.
* Bachelor's degree in relevant field required; master’s degree preferred.

  

All candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S.; no visa sponsorships are offered.


This position is currently based in our New Jersey office, though we are open to a fully remote arrangement for the right candidate. Regardless of location, candidates should expect to travel domestically and internationally.


Applicants should submit their cover letter, resume, relevant work samples, and a list of 4 references (pastoral, supervisor, direct report, peer)

Description:
**BACKGROUND**

**The Organization**


Since 1984, STRIVE has helped individuals facing significant barriers to employment gain access to meaningful careers, economic mobility, and long\-term opportunity. Through its proven Five\-Pillar Model, STRIVE combines career readiness, occupational skills training, career coaching, job placement assistance, and lifetime support to help participants secure and sustain employment. Over four decades, STRIVE and its affiliates have served more than 90,000 individuals nationwide.


Today, STRIVE operates direct\-service sites in New York City, Atlanta, Birmingham, New Orleans, Northern New Jersey, and will open a new site in Houston in Spring 2027\. Additionally, STRIVE supports a growing network of partner\-operated programs across the country. The organization has earned national recognition for achieving strong outcomes while serving individuals who face some of the greatest barriers to employment, including housing instability, justice\-system involvement, and substance use recovery.


STRIVE is now embarking on an ambitious next chapter. Guided by a multi\-year growth plan, developed with the support of The Bridgespan Group, the organization aims to serve 20,000 individuals annually by 2036 through a growing network of direct\-operated and partner\-operated sites, positioning STRIVE as the nation's leading employment partner for highly barriered jobseekers. Over the next decade, STRIVE expects to serve approximately 110,000 individuals, generating an estimated $1\.5 billion in wage gains and transforming economic opportunity for families and communities across the country.


To achieve this vision, STRIVE is investing in organizational capacity, fundraising, public funding strategy, technology, evaluation, and national infrastructure. The organization's next Chief Development Officer will play a critical leadership role in securing the resources, partnerships, and strategic investments necessary to fuel this growth and national expansion.


To learn more about STRIVE, please visit www.strive.org

**The Position**


The Chief Development Officer reports to the Chief Executive Officer, serves as a member of STRIVE's Executive Leadership Team, and leads the organization's Development function.

The next Chief Development Officer will focus on accelerating growth, expanding revenue, strengthening organizational positioning, and securing transformational investments that support STRIVE's long\-term vision for national scale.


Over the coming years, STRIVE must demonstrate its ability to expand into new markets, support partner\-operated sites, increase public funding, activate local fundraising ecosystems, and sustain a growing national network. The Chief Development Officer will serve as the architect of that fundraising strategy, translating organizational ambitions into actionable revenue plans and ensuring the organization has the philanthropic, public, and private resources necessary to achieve its goals.


This leader will partner closely with the CEO, Executive Directors, board members, local advisory boards, and external funding partners to identify opportunities, cultivate strategic relationships, and secure transformational investments. The successful candidate will combine strategic vision with disciplined execution, proactively identifying new funding opportunities, mobilizing stakeholders around clear fundraising priorities, and ensuring accountability for results across a complex and growing organization. Our wide range of programs, spanning social services, education, and recreation, reflects our mission to build a more connected, inclusive, and thriving community for all. **ABOUT THE ROLE:**

The Program Director is responsible for the overall leadership, daily operations, program development, staff supervision, community outreach, and contract compliance of our Neighborhood Naturally Occurring Retirement Community WithOut Walls (NNORC WOW) Supportive Services Program serving parts of Floral Park, New Hyde Park and Bellerose, Queens. This role reports directly to the Senior Program Director. **ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES:****Role Responsibilities:*** Provides overall leadership and day\-to\-day oversight of the NNORC WOW Supportive Services Program ensuring high\-quality services and programming that responds to participant and community needs.
* Supervise, support, and evaluate a team of administrative staff, social workers, interns, consulting RNs, instructors, and volunteers, and promotes professional development.. Manages attendance for all.
* Meets with potential new members to explain services available and to assess client needs; provides case management and case assistance via telephone, office or home visits as appropriate.
* Ensures program and staff meet standards and adhere to policies and procedures as set forth by funding sources including, but not limited to, the New York City Department for the Aging, New York State Office for the Aging and UJA Federation.
* Responsible for timely completion of all internal and external reports; tracks program utilization via the departmental dashboard, and service outcomes through satisfaction surveys, needs assessments and participant feedback to guide programming and quality improvement.
* Develops and implements outreach strategies to support program growth, including strategies to reach a diverse, underserved population.
* Builds and maintains valuable relationships with local legislative representatives, other community based organizations, Senior Advisory/Partners Board members, community nursing partners, local hospitals and rehabilitation centers as well as other divisions within the agency.
* Facilitates quarterly meetings of the Senior Advisory/Partners Board.
* Works with program/department staff to create monthly and bi\-monthly calendars of events and programming for distribution to the community.
* Participates in regularly scheduled meetings of the Older Adult Services Department Program Directors, and department\-wide quarterly and annual meetings.
* Assists with budget development, grant writing and contract renewals.
* Other duties as assigned.

 **Performance \& Organizational Excellence*** Participates in the agency's performance management process by establishing annual goals, completing mid\-year and end\-of\-year evaluations, and engaging in ongoing performance discussions with supervisors and supervisees.
* Completes documentation, data entry, and required reports accurately and on time in accordance with agency standards, funder requirements, and established deadlines, including updates to agency systems, dashboards, and tracking tools.
* Completes required annual professional development activities to maintain and strengthen clinical knowledge, professional skills, and overall job performance.
* Uses program and service data to improve performance by participating in data review and discussion during supervision, department meetings, reporting activities, and other quality improvement efforts, including surveys and feedback activities, as applicable.

 **QUALIFICATIONS \& KEY ATTRIBUTES:****Minimum Qualifications*** Master of Social Work (MSW) from an accredited program and current New York State LMSW license required.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible program management experience in a community\-based social service setting, preferably within the field of Aging.
* SIFI certified, or SIFI eligible and willing to obtain certification, with the ability to supervise social work interns.

jobs.description:
**Boston College Introduction**  

Founded in 1863, Boston College is a Jesuit, Catholic university located six miles from downtown Boston with an enrollment of 9,654 full\-time undergraduates and 5,072 graduate and professional students. Ranked 37 among national universities, Boston College has 923 full\-time and 1,336 FTE faculty, 2,822 non\-faculty employees, an operating budget of $1\.4 billion, and an endowment in excess of $3\.9 billion.

 **Job Description** **About Boston College**

  

Founded in 1863, Boston College is one of the 27 Jesuit, Catholic universities in the United States. It is dedicated to the pursuit of truth and the use of knowledge in service to the common good. The University’s mission is rooted in a world view that values rigorous intellectual development and ethical formation.Institutional Overview \& Mission Alignment.


Boston College is embarking on a transformative initiative with the establishment of the **Krantz Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Ethics, and Humanity**. Enabled by a major gift from University Trustee Jason Krantz '95, P'23, and Keely (Fitzgerald) Krantz '95, P'23, the Institute will leverage BC’s formative and ethical strengths as a Jesuit, Catholic university to explore the opportunities, implications, and pitfalls of artificial intelligence.


Inspired by Pope Leo’s recently published encyclical, *Magnifica Humanitas*, which underscores education’s role in an era of rapid technological change, the Institute brings BC’s rich heritage of thoughtful reflection and discernment into a lively engagement with the promise and perils of a particularly transformative technology. The institute aims to inform emerging discussion of AI and to instill in students the judgment, wisdom, and critical thinking necessary to become moral leaders and creators of AI, ensuring that humanistic values and ethics remain foundational to the world's evolving approach to AI.


**Position Overview \& Strategic Direction**


Reporting to the Provost and Dean of Faculties, the Executive Director will build an Institute that will position Boston College as a national and global leader in teaching, research, and discussion about the opportunities and implications of artificial intelligence as well as to scale foundational and applied AI initiatives across all nine of the schools and colleges at Boston College. Working closely with faculty colleagues, academic leadership, and external partners, the successful candidate will build this early\-stage platform into a sustainable, world\-class hub of institutional excellence.


The Executive Director will be charged with driving three primary goals:


* **Convene Global Thought Leaders:** Organize world\-class conferences and symposia at Boston College to explore AI’s potential impact on education and humanity.**The Executive Director will partner with academics across and beyond campus to sustain a lively and ongoing conversation about AI, ethics, and humanity.**


* **Cultivate Student Formation and Leadership:** Offer fellowships, internships, and experiential learning opportunities to equip BC students with the experience and expertise to participate thoughtfully in how the world should engage with AI.
* **Advance Curricular \& Internal Innovation:** Imagine and implement campus\-wide AI programs, support the integration of AI\-related topics across disciplines, and award internal seed grants to support innovation in applying AI to teaching, research, and higher education operations.


**Core Programmatic Pillars**


The Executive Director will develop, operationalize, and guide the institute's core strategic pillars to catalyze campus engagement with AI and to establish a clear framework for investment and prioritization with an ambition to inform national and global conversations about AI:


* **AI \& Human Flourishing:** Exploring AI in light of fundamental questions about ethics and human dignity, and drawing on the University’s distinctive strengths in the humanities.
* **AI \& Democracy:** Examining AI’s various effects on government and public life, in the United States and beyond.
* **AI \& the Economy:** Guiding organizations on how to responsibly leverage AI and engaging with industry leaders (including partnering with the Carroll School of Management and the 2027 Finance Conference).
* **AI \& Health Care:** Investigating how AI can improve healthcare outcomes while recognizing emerging threats to human\-centered care for the vulnerable.
* **AI \& Formative Education:** Imagining new possibilities for BC’s distinctive approach to teaching and learning in the context of the AI revolution.
* **AI \& Faith:** Rooted in BC's Jesuit, Catholic heritage and mission, this pillar is at once the Institute's clearest differentiator and an area where Boston College is called to provide leadership to colleges, schools, and other faith\-based organizations.

Within each pillar, the Executive Director will develop a robust set of mechanisms appropriate to the theme; examples include research grants, undergraduate fellowships, curriculum integration, industry partnerships, conferences and symposia, and visiting scholars.


**Key Responsibilities and Scope**


* **Strategic \& Operational Leadership:** Partner with faculty and academic leadership to execute long\-term strategies, balancing academic priorities with rigorous operational execution.
* **Interdisciplinary Integration:** Connect technical AI researchers with diverse fields, including business, law, education, social work, nursing, and the humanities, to advance an expansive portfolio of creative pedagogy and use\-inspired research.
* **Faculty Support:** Facilitate large\-scale, multi\-investigator research proposals and support the recruitment, retention, and mentorship of senior faculty, tenure\-track hires, postdoctoral scholars, and students.
* **External Partnerships \& Public Voice:** Build strong partnerships with non\-profit organizations, for\-profit c

**Executive Director**  

Conservation Voters for Idaho \| Salary Range: $110,000\-$120,000 \| Hybrid \- Boise, Idaho  

  

**The Opportunity**  

Conservation Voters for Idaho is looking for an accomplished, collaborative, and mission\-driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director.  

  

CVI protects Idaho’s environment and quality of life by informing, engaging, and empowering people who care about our natural heritage and healthy communities. Through CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees, the organization works to build political power for conservation and advance priorities that protect what makes Idaho special.  

  

This is an opportunity to lead an established and respected organization into its next chapter. CVI is looking for an Executive Director who knows that strong results start with strong people leadership and who can pair that with successful fundraising, strategic thinking, coalition\-building, and political judgment.  

  

The Executive Director will lead CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees, working in partnership with the appropriate Boards of Directors, senior leaders, staff, donors, funders, partners, and supporters to move the organizations' missions forward.  

  

**The Leader We Are Looking For**  

CVI's next Executive Director will be a proven organizational leader who builds trust, develops people, and creates the conditions for employees to do their best work.  

They will be collaborative, emotionally intelligent, adaptable, and approachable, while also being comfortable setting clear expectations, addressing difficult issues, making decisions, and holding people accountable.  

They will also be a strong relationship\-builder who is comfortable moving between conversations with staff, donors, funders, Board members, conservation partners, community leaders, elected officials, candidates, and other stakeholders.  

CVI operates in a complex political environment. The next Executive Director does not need to have spent their entire career in Idaho or in the conservation movement, but they do need the political judgment, relationship skills, and strategic thinking to build alliances and move conservation priorities forward.  

**Key Areas of Leadership*** **Lead People and Culture \-** Build and sustain a healthy, high\-performing workplace grounded in trust, respect, collaboration, accountability, and clear communication. Develop staff, provide meaningful feedback, be open and receptive to receiving feedback, address performance concerns, and support professional growth.
* **Provide Strategic and Political Leadership \-** Lead the work of CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees and guide effective political, advocacy, and electoral strategies that strengthen political power for conservation.
* **Drive Fundraising and Resource Development \-** Build strong relationships with donors, foundations, and institutional funders; take an active role in significant asks; secure financial support; and help diversify the organizations' funding base.
* **Build Relationships, Coalitions, and Partnerships \-** Develop productive relationships with conservation organizations, community partners, state and national partners, elected officials, candidates, supporters, and stakeholders across a range of political perspectives.
* **Partner with the Boards of Directors \-** Support effective governance through strong communication, strategic alignment, transparency, and organizational accountability.
* **Steward the Organization \-** Take responsibility for financial health, operational effectiveness, compliance, and long\-term sustainability.

**What You’ll Bring**  

Strong candidates will have senior or executive leadership experience in a nonprofit, mission\-driven, public\-sector, or similarly complex organization, along with a track record of leading and developing staff.  

They should also bring experience building trusted relationships, raising funds and developing resources, thinking strategically, communicating clearly, and making sound decisions, including when the issues are difficult.  

Experience with nonprofit executive leadership, Boards of Directors, coalition\-building, advocacy or electoral work, public policy, and environmental or conservation issues is highly valued. Familiarity with Idaho's political, nonprofit, conservation, or advocacy landscape is preferred.  

 CVI is also looking for a leader who demonstrates cultural competency and a commitment to racial equity, justice, and inclusive organizational practices.  

  

**Compensation \& Benefits**  

The salary range for the Executive Director is **$110,000\-$120,000**, depending on experience and qualifications.  

CVI offers a competitive benefits package, including employer\-paid employee premiums for health, dental, and vision insurance. Benefits also include a SIMPLE IRA with an employer match of up to 3%, flexible spending and dependent\-care accounts, a health reimbursement account, short\-term disability coverage, an Employee Assistance Program, and an annual cell\-phone reimbursement.  

CVI also offers generous paid time off, personal days, paid holidays, Summer Fridays between Memorial Day and Labor Day, a paid bonus week between Christmas and New Year's Day, sick leave, and additional paid leave benefits. Eligible employees may also qualify for a one\-month paid sabbatical after five years of continuous service.

CVI uses a hybrid work model, and the Executive Director is based in Boise, Idaho.
  

This role requires flexibility outside standard business hours. Periodic evening and weekend work should be expected for Board and organizational meetings, fundraising and community events, legislative and political activities, campaigns, and other mission\-related priorities.

**Executive Director**

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and sustainability of AVENUES for Northeast Missouri. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director provides strategic direction, financial oversight, resource development, staff leadership, and community representation to advance the organization's mission of supporting survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, and related crimes.

* Promote transparency, accountability, and ethical decision\-making.
* Provide trauma\-informed leadership and support while remaining calm, professional, and respectful in challenging situations involving staff, survivors, community partners, and stakeholders.
* Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and model behaviors that support the agency's mission, values, and ethical standards.
* Make objective decisions based on facts, agency policies, organizational needs, and the safety and well\-being of survivors, staff, and the agency rather than personal opinions, relationships, or conflicts.

* Oversee agency finances, budgeting, and fiscal management.

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative of AVENUES.
* Build and maintain relationships with community partners, government agencies, funders, donors, and stakeholders.
* Promote awareness of agency services and the impact of domestic and sexual violence within the communities served.

**Compliance \& Governance**

* Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, contracts, and grant requirements.
* Oversee policy development and implementation.
* Work collaboratively with the Board of Directors to support effective governance and strategic planning.

**Preferred Education**

Bachelor's degree in:

* Social Work
* Human Services
* Nonprofit Management
* Public Administration
* Business Administration
* Psychology
* Or a related field

Relevant experience may be substituted for formal education.

**Preferred Experience**

* Leadership or management experience in a nonprofit, social service, victim service, healthcare, education, or related organization.
* Grant writing and fundraising experience.
* Financial management and budget oversight experience.
* Staff supervision and team development experience.
* Public relations, community engagement, or government relations experience.
* Knowledge of domestic violence, sexual assault, victim services, or trauma\-informed practices preferred.

**Core Competencies**

* Mission\-driven leadership
* Grant writing and fundraising
* Financial management
* Strategic planning
* Communication and public relations
* Staff development and supervision
* Relationship building
* Problem\-solving and decision\-making
* Transparency and accountability
* Commitment to employee wellness and organizational sustainability

**Desired Leadership Style**

The ideal candidate is a compassionate, collaborative leader who:

* Understands nonprofit funding and operations.
* Communicates openly and honestly.
* Builds trust with staff, survivors, and community partners.
* Supports employee autonomy and avoids micromanagement.
* Values work\-life balance and staff well\-being.
* Demonstrates a genuine commitment to the mission of AVENUES.

**Position Details**

**Position:** Executive Director  
**Employment Status:** Full\-Time, Exempt  
**Salary:** $75,000–$80,000 annually, commensurate with qualifications and experience  
**Primary Location:** AVENUES for Northeast Missouri, Inc. Main Office — Hannibal, Missouri  
**Reports To:** Board of Directors  
**Application Period:** Open Until Filled

**Schedule \& Travel**

The standard work schedule is **Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.** AVENUES supports a flexible work environment that recognizes the importance of work\-life balance while ensuring the leadership and operational needs of the agency are met.

Some evening or weekend availability may be required based on agency needs, community events, meetings, or other Executive Director responsibilities. Regular holiday work is not required.

Some travel is required for agency business, including travel throughout AVENUES’ service area, meetings, trainings, and community engagement activities. Approved business mileage is reimbursed in accordance with agency policy.

**Benefits**

AVENUES offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

* Health insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Vacation time
* Sick leave
* Personal time off
* Flexible work schedule with an emphasis on work\-life balance

Qualified applicants should submit a **resume and cover letter*

*NAMI\-RC Board of Directors*

**Classification:**

*Full\-Time (40hrs/week)*

The National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) is the nation’s largest grassroots mental health organization dedicated to building better lives for the millions of Americans affected by mental illness. NAMI Richland County, established in July 2001, is the local affiliate of the NAMI organization, serving families and individuals through education, support, and advocacy.

**Our Mission**: NAMI provides advocacy, education, support, and public awareness so that all individuals and families affected by mental illness can build better lives.

**Our Vision**: NAMI envisions a world where all people affected by mental illness live healthy, fulfilling lives supported by a community that cares.

**Our Values:**

* **Hope:** We believe in the possibility of recovery, wellness, and the potential in all of us.
* **Inclusion:** We embrace diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives.
* **Empowerment:** We promote confidence, self\-efficacy, and service to our mission.
* **Compassion:** We practice respect, kindness, and empathy.
* **Fairness:** We fight for equity and justice.

Overview

The Executive Director serves as the visionary leader and chief administrator of NAMI Richland County. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director is responsible for the organization’s financial health, strategic growth, and the successful delivery of mental health support and advocacy programs. This role requires a sophisticated blend of fiscal management, community partnership development, and compassionate team leadership.

This position requires a balance of high\-level strategy, fiscal rigor, and grassroots community engagement. · Execute full\-cycle internal payroll, including the calculation and filing of all local, state, and federal payroll taxes.

Executive Director \- UCAN City Mission

Position Summary


The Executive Director serves as the chief executive leader of UCAN City Mission, providing spiritual, strategic, and operational leadership to advance the Mission’s Christ\-centered purpose.


This role sets both short\-term priorities and long\-term vision, ensuring the organization remains focused, sustainable, and responsive to the evolving needs of the community. The Executive Director oversees all aspects of ministry operations, including staff leadership, program effectiveness, financial stewardship, facilities oversight, and community engagement.


As the Mission expands to serve both men and women with children across multiple locations, the Executive Director will guide this growth while maintaining excellence in care, safety, and program outcomes.


The Executive Director leads the Mission through a team of key leaders, equipping and overseeing those responsible for day\-to\-day ministry operations while ensuring strong alignment, accountability, and effectiveness across all areas. The Executive Director remains closely connected to frontline ministry—maintaining visibility with staff and guests and staying informed of the realities, challenges, and opportunities within Mission programs.


This role requires a leader who operates at both the strategic and relational levels—guiding the organization through others while remaining present and connected to those they serve.

Spiritual \& Ministry Leadership


* Model and cultivate a Christ\-centered culture grounded in the Mission’s Statement of Faith
* Provide spiritual leadership to staff and program direction, ensuring ministry is meaningfully integrated into all services
* Support discipleship, restoration, and life transformation through both compassionate care and clear expectations for growth
* Establish a ministry environment that balances grace, accountability, and personal responsibility, recognizing the complexities of addiction, trauma, and mental health
* Ensure all services are delivered in alignment with the Mission’s Christian identity while integrating spiritual formation with program structure to create pathways toward lasting change

Strategic Leadership \& Organizational Direction

* Address conflict directly and constructively, strengthening trust and organizational effectiveness
* Ensure leaders are equipped to manage staff and programs with consistency and excellence

Operations, Policy \& Program Oversight

* Ensure the development, implementation, and consistent enforcement of policies, procedures, and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and safety standards

Guest Care, Safety \& Program Integrity

* Promote an environment that is safe, respectful, and conducive to transformation

Facilities \& Environment Oversight


* Ensure all facilities are safe, clean, and well\-maintained for both guests and staff

* Maintain environments that reflect dignity, order, and care

Financial Management \& Resource Development


* Develop and manage the annual budget in partnership with the Board

* Lead and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy, including donor engagement, grants, and community partnerships

Board \& Community Relations


* Serve as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, providing clear and timely reporting on operations, finances, and outcomes

* Serve as a visible and credible public voice for the Mission, representing its work to churches, donors, community partners, and public stakeholders
* Build and strengthen relationships that advance the Mission’s reach and sustainability, including volunteer engagement aligned with Mission programs

Minimum Qualifications


* Bachelor’s Degree required
* Demonstrated commitment to Jesus Christ, including willingness to affirm and sign the Mission’s Statement of Faith
* Proven experience supervising staff and leading teams
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
* Submit to background/criminal history and fingerprint check

Preferred Qualifications \& Competencies


* Experience in nonprofit, ministry, or human services lead

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development leads Eden Centers for Hope and Healing’s comprehensive fundraising and development strategy, with responsibility for growing and diversifying contributed revenue through individual giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, institutional and government funding, fundraising campaigns, events, and community engagement.

As Eden Centers’ senior development leader, the Director develops and executes the organization’s annual fundraising strategy, cultivates and stewards key donor and funder relationships, oversees development operations and staff, and ensures fundraising efforts are aligned with organizational priorities and long\-term sustainability. The Director also plays a key role in Eden Centers’ capital campaign and expansion efforts, helping to cultivate and secure major philanthropic investments to support the organization’s continued growth.

The Director works closely with the CEO, COO, executive leadership, finance team, and Board of Directors and serves as a trusted advisor on fundraising strategy, revenue opportunities, donor engagement, and external positioning. This position reports directly to the COO and supervises the development team, including Grant Coordinator and a Grant Writer.

**Fundraising Strategy, Revenue \& Donor Development**

* Develop and execute Eden Centers’ annual fundraising plan in alignment with the organizational budget, strategic plan, and programmatic priorities.
* Lead efforts to meet annual contributed revenue goals and grow and diversify funding from individual donors, major gifts, corporate partners, foundations, events, campaigns, and community giving.
* Monitor fundraising performance against annual goals and budget projections, identify gaps and opportunities, and adjust strategy throughout the year.
* Work closely with the CEO, COO, and finance team on fundraising projections, revenue tracking, reconciliation, and the development department budget.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, major gift prospects, corporate partners, sponsors, and other supporters.
* Develop strategies to strengthen donor acquisition, retention, engagement, and increased giving.
* Manage key donor relationships through meetings, tours, personalized outreach, solicitations, impact updates, and ongoing stewardship.
* Provide regular fundraising reports and updates to the CEO, COO, executive leadership, and Board of Directors.

**Capital Campaign, Grants \& Institutional Giving**

* Play a key leadership role in Eden Centers’ capital campaign and expansion efforts, working with the CEO,COO, Board, campaign leadership, to secure significant philanthropic investments.
* Identify and cultivate capital campaign and major gift prospects and develop individualized strategies for cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* Develop campaign proposals, case statements, presentations, and other donor\-facing materials and maintain accurate tracking of prospects, commitments, and campaign progress.
* Lead Eden Centers’ institutional funding strategy across foundation, corporate, local, state, and federal funding opportunities.
* Oversee and contribute directly to grant applications and reports, particularly complex, high\-priority, and government funding opportunities.
* Coordinate with clinical, finance, and executive staff to develop accurate narratives, budgets, outcomes, and supporting materials.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with current and prospective institutional funders.

**Events, Communications \& Community Engagement**

* Lead strategy and execution for Eden Centers’ fundraising events and campaigns, including our annual fall fundraiser, Building Dreams, GiveNOLA Day, and other annual appeals.
* Establish event and campaign revenue goals, budgets, sponsorship strategies, timelines, and outreach plans and evaluate performance following each initiative.
* Oversee sponsorship outreach, donor recognition, event communications, mailing lists, logistics, and post\-event stewardship.
* Oversee Eden Centers’ external communications and storytelling, including donor appeals, newsletters, impact reports, campaign materials, and other fundraising communications.
* Oversee Eden Centers’ digital communications platforms, including Mailchimp, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and the organizational website, ensuring content is current, consistent, engaging, and mission\-aligned.
* Work with clinical staff to gather impact data and organizational updates and ensure survivor\-related communications are trauma\-informed, survivor\-centered, and protective of confidentiality.
* Oversee third\-party fundraising initiatives, community donation drives, and in\-kind donations, including maintaining current needs and online wish lists and stewarding in\-kind donors and community partners.
* Represent Eden Centers at donor meetings, tours, community events, funder meetings, and other external engagements.

**Development Operations \& Data Management**

* Oversee NEON CRM and maintain accurate and organized donor, prospect, gift, campaign, and engagement records.
* Ensure gifts and in\-kind contributions are appropriately recorded, acknowledged, tracked, and reconciled with finance.
* Maintain standards for donor data, database cleanliness, gift processing, and development documentation.
* Create reports and dashboards to track revenue, donor acquisition and retention, major gifts, campaigns, grants, and other key fundraising metrics.
* Manage donor segmentation and mailing lists for appeals, events, newsletters, and stewardship.
* Maintain an organized development calendar and systems for donor follow\-up, grant deadlines, campaigns, events, and other department priorities.
* Continuously improve development processes and systems to increase efficiency, consistency, and long\-term sustainability.

jobs.title: Interim Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
**Kinexus Group is seeking an accomplished executive to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer during an important period of organizational transition, anticipated to last up to six months. The Interim CEO will provide stability and continuity during the evaluation of the governance structure, while maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders. The Interim CEO will collaborate with the Chief Elected Officials Board, Kinexus Group Board of Directors, and counties to ensure transparency, accountability, effective communication and continued organizational momentum.**

  


**OUR ORGANIZATION:**



Kinexus Group, recognized as one of Nonprofit Times 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2026 Best Nonprofits to Work For, is a cutting\-edge community development organization with growing initiatives to create an economically thriving Michigan. We are change agents who create solutions for business, workforce, and community challenges to promote economic vitality.



Kinexus Group is a dynamic, steadily growing organization committed to advancing its mission and impact across Michigan. We are seeking a mission\-driven, seasoned, and strategic executive who can inspire teams, strengthen operations, and drive enterprise\-level results. The ideal candidate is a systems thinker with strong process orientation and demonstrated experience scaling organizations, leading high\-performing management teams, and operating within a geographically distributed staffing model. A proven ability to cultivate a performance\-driven culture among diverse and talented professionals is essential.



The Interim Chief Executive Officer will provide visionary leadership and enterprise stewardship for Kinexus Group by aligning and advancing the strategic direction of the enterprise to include the corporate team and its subsidiary organizations. This executive will align and support multiple subsidiaries delivering critical services across the state, leading a workforce of nearly 100 dedicated employees.


**OUR DESIRED OUTCOMES:**



The Interim CEO of Kinexus Group is responsible for leading the enterprise toward its mission of creating transformative economic, workforce, and community impact across Southwest Michigan and beyond. The CEO ensures organizational Health, Integration, and Impact, and serves as the primary driver of the organization's strategy, external presence, culture, and long\-term sustainability.



The Interim CEO leads Kinexus Group and its subsidiaries as a unified, innovative, and results\-oriented system that delivers bold solutions to complex workforce, economic and community challenges.


**WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU:**



The Interim CEO must be a visionary, entrepreneurial leader who inspires trust, cultivates strong partnerships, and drives measurable outcomes. This role requires a strategic thinker with the confidence to mobilize teams, foster innovation, and steward resources effectively.



The successful Interim will be a connector across government, private industry, philanthropy, and community partners – elevating the organization's visibility and expanding its influence. They will partner closely with the corporate leadership team, Chief Elected Official Board, Kinexus Group Board and legal counsel to ensure high\-performing operations and aligned execution.


**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**


**Enterprise Leadership \& Vision**


* Provide strategic leadership and clarity of vision for Kinexus Group and alignment for all subsidiary entities.
* Supervises the subsidiary chief executives in conjunction and consultation with the subsidiary board of directors' chair of the board.
* Refine governance documents in partnership with the Kinexus Group Board of Directors and CEOB to reflect the current structure of the organization, including the interlocal agreement, bylaws, and other foundational documents.
* Champion organizational health, mission alignment, and strategic coherence across the enterprise.
* Lead development, communication, and execution of the long\-term strategic plan.
* Ensure bold innovation and continuous improvement remain core to enterprise culture.


**Board \& Governance Engagement**


* Serve as the primary liaison to the Kinexus Group Board of Directors and Chief Elected Officials Board ensuring transparency, accountability, and timely communication.
* Provide thought leadership to the Boards regarding strategy, risk, performance, and future opportunities.
* Ensure strong governance practices across subsidiaries and compliance with all legal, financial, and regulatory obligations, especially the legal separation between the subsidiaries and the parent organization.
* Ensure operational control to subsidiary leadership is implemented and followed within Kinexus Group board approved parameters, and that the subsidiary boards govern, and management teams operate
* Preserve alignment with Kinexus Group strategy while preserving subsidiary operational autonomy
* Serve on subsidiary boards representing Kinexus Group as the member or parent organization


**External Relations, Advocacy \& Partnerships**


* Represent Kinexus Group with federal, state, and local governments; community leaders; industry partners; philanthropy; and the public and in conjunction and coordination with the chief executives of each subsidiary.
* Serve as the chief spokesperson and ambassador for the organization, elevating the enterprise's voice and influence.
* Build strong, trust\-based relationships with funding agencies, policymakers, and partner organizations.
* Advocate for policies and investments that support workforce, community, and economic development.


**Enterprise Strategy, Performance \& Integration**


* Oversee execution of enterprise\-wide strategy, ensuring alignment across all subsidiaries.
* Ensure the implementation and adherence to the unique business model where the subsidiary boards have fiduciary, legal and operational autonomy within the Kinexus Group governance
